gp.text: Gross margin decreased 0.2 percentage points primarily driven by the amortization of certain intangible assets resulting from the AZEK acquisition of $16.0 million, which was partially offset by higher gross margin in our Siding & Trim and Australia & New Zealand segments.

oi.text: Net income increased 67% due to h igher operating income and lower other expense as the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 included an $11.6 million non-cash loss on our interest rate swap. This was partially offset by higher interest and income tax expense.

rd.text: Research and development expenses (“R&D”) expenses increased $7.2 million primarily due to the allocation of $6.1 million of R&D expenses which were not allocated to our segments prior to the second quarter of fiscal year 2026.

ga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses (“SG&A”) increased 89% and as a percentage of sales increased 2.7 percentage points. As a percentage of sales, this increase was primarily due to the amortization of certain intangible assets resulting from the AZEK acquisition of $61.6 million, partially offset by lower labor costs and professional fees.

sga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses (“SG&A”) increased 89% and as a percentage of sales increased 2.7 percentage points. As a percentage of sales, this increase was primarily due to the amortization of certain intangible assets resulting from the AZEK acquisition of $61.6 million, partially offset by lower labor costs and professional fees.

pretax.text: We define Adjusted Net Income as net income before legacy items such as asbestos related expenses and adjustments, and AICF interest income and significant non-recurring items, such as restructuring gain or expenses, acquisition and pre-close financing related costs, inventory fair value adjustment, amortization of intangible assets resulting from AZEK acquisition, as well as share-based compensation expense and adjustments to tax expenses.

tax.text: Income tax expense increased 96%, while the effective tax rate increased 3.5 percentage points. The increase in tax expense reflects higher income before income taxes compared to fiscal year 2026, while the higher effective tax rate was primarily driven by discrete items.

net.text: Net income increased 67% due to h igher operating income and lower other expense as the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 included an $11.6 million non-cash loss on our interest rate swap. This was partially offset by higher interest and income tax expense.

ocf.heading: Cash Provided by Operating Activities
ocf.text: The $137.1 million increase in cash provided by operating activities is primarily driven by higher operating income generated by increased net sales. This increase was partially offset by lower cash provided by working capital, principally reflecting less favorable changes in accounts receivable and accounts payable.

da.text: We define Adjusted EBITDA as net income before interest, net, other expense (income), net, income tax expense and depreciation and amortization, and items such as asbestos related expenses and adjustments, share-based compensation expense, and significant non-recurring items, such as restructuring gain and expenses, acquisition related expenses and inventory fair value adjustment. Adjusted EBITDA Margin is equal to Adjusted EBITDA divided by net sales.

sbc.text: We define Adjusted Net Income as net income before legacy items such as asbestos related expenses and adjustments, and AICF interest income and significant non-recurring items, such as restructuring gain or expenses, acquisition and pre-close financing related costs, inventory fair value adjustment, amortization of intangible assets resulting from AZEK acquisition, as well as share-based compensation expense and adjustments to tax expenses.

wc.text: • These measures do not reflect changes in, or cash requirements for, our working capital needs;

capex.text: In addition, we provide Free Cash Flow, which is a non-GAAP financial measure that we define as net cash provided by (used in) operating activities less purchases of property, plant and equipment plus any proceeds on sale of property, plant and equipment. gp.text: Gross margin increased 6.6 percentage points primarily driven by a $47.9 million inventory step-up adjustment related to recording the acquired inventory of AZEK at fair value in the second quarter of fiscal year 2026 which did not repeat in the current corresponding period. This was partially offset by higher intangible asset amortization following the finalization of the purchase price allocation related to the AZEK acquisition. Intangible asset amortization expense was $16.0 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 compared to $12.4 million in the prior corresponding period.

oi.text: Net income from continuing operations was $149.8 million compared to a net loss from continuing operations of $64.3 million in the prior corresponding period, primarily due to higher operating income, partially offset by higher income tax expense.

costs.text: Acquisition and divestiture related expenses decreased 88% primarily due to lower professional service fees and labor costs, including severance and retention costs and expenses associated with the accelerated vesting of certain stock awards in connection with the AZEK acquisition. Acquisition related expenses were $9.7 million and $128.9 million in the second quarter of fiscal years 2027 and 2026, respectively, and include costs associated with the AZEK acquisition and ongoing integration activities. The second quarter of fiscal year 2027 also included $5.2 million of divestiture related expenses

rd.text: Research and development expenses (“R&D”) expenses increased $5.9 million primarily due to the allocation of R&D expenses which were not allocated to our segments prior to the second quarter of fiscal year 2026.

ga.text: Selling, general and administrative expenses (“SG&A”) increased 21% and as a percentage of sales decreased 0.4 percentage points. As a percentage of sales, this decrease was primarily due to lower discretionary marketing spend and lower labor costs, partially offset by higher stock compensation expense and higher amortization of intangible assets resulting from the AZEK acquisition. Higher stock compensation expense in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 was mainly due to timing of grants and a larger stock price decrease in the prior corresponding period. Amortization from the AZEK acquisition was $61.5 million in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 compared with $36.3 million in the prior corresponding period.

Higher stock compensation expense in the second quarter of fiscal year 2027 was mainly due to timing of grants and a larger stock price decrease in the prior corresponding period. lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
